card.name: Inaba White Rabbit
card.effect: This card cannot be Special Summoned. This card returns to the owner's hand during the End Phase of the turn that this card is Normal Summoned or flipped face-up. This monster attacks your opponent's Life Points directly.

behavior: Rejects Special Summon attempts as a summoning condition, independently of monster-effect negation.
Registers Normal Summon, Flip Summon and effect-based face-up transitions with a durable UID/zone-epoch binding.
At the same turn's End Phase, returns a still face-up, non-negated instance to its physical owner's private hand, even after control changes.
Does not return a card that left the field, changed to face-down, or was re-entered as a new zone epoch; a fresh face-up event creates a new marker.
Allows direct-attack permission while face-up and not effect-negated, even if the opposing team controls monsters.
Does not discard hand overflow; the shared End Phase hand-limit flow remains responsible for the limit of six.

covers: Normal Summon, Flip Summon and effect-based face-up transition
End Phase timing and physical-owner hand routing
control change without loss of physical ownership
face-down, removed, stale-zone and fresh-reentry behavior
direct attack with opposing monsters, face-up condition and effect negation
duplicate summon/End Phase receipts and JSON restoration
hand overflow deferred to existing End Phase flow
Deck 20/30, Extra Deck 5 and 3+3 shared zones

integrationBoundary: Isolated TagDuel adapter only. Inaba White Rabbit is not added to cardMetadata, cardCatalog, cardCertifications, release allowlist, the central resolver, or Discord commands. The test injects an already-admitted effect-monster fixture ID; the production passcode remains 77084837. Central Spirit/End Phase wiring and direct-attack integration remain pending the explicit M61 resolver handoff.
limitations: End Phase ordering is supplied by the future resolver integration; this adapter does not alter the shared End Phase pipeline.
Direct-attack permission is a card-specific predicate; the engine still owns battle-phase, attack-count, and declaration validation.
No real Discord gateway/guild session, production database, player data, or hosting credentials were used.
